forces.title: Drugstores leverage e-commerce to gain market share
forces.description: Multichannel retailers, particularly supermarkets and drugstores, are outperforming online-only retailers in the Netherlands' e-commerce market. This trend reflects their success in strengthening digital capabilities and integrating online convenience with physical store advantages like click-and-collect, providing a robust and growing channel for branded OTC medicines and self-care products.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Pharmacists' expanded clinical role enhances primary care
forces.description: The expansion of pharmacists' clinical role through the Common Conditions Service in Ireland marks a significant structural change. This development strengthens community pharmacy's position as a key component of primary care and pharmacy-led health management, which is central to self-medication guidance and the accessibility of OTC medicines.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Healthcare policy supports community-based care
forces.description: Irish healthcare policy increasingly prioritizes community-based and home-based models of care, which elevates the strategic importance of community pharmacies. This ongoing shift supports pharmacists playing an increasingly vital role in frontline healthcare delivery, thereby bolstering the ecosystem for self-medication and branded OTC medicines.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Stronger retail spending on pharmaceuticals and self-care
forces.description: Despite a challenging retail environment, the 'Pharmaceuticals, Medical & Cosmetic Articles' subsector in Ireland is demonstrating stronger performance. This indicates resilient consumer demand for health-related products, including OTC medicines and self-care items, suggesting a positive consumer spending trend that benefits the IN060701 sector.

forces.title: Continued consolidation and M&A activity in community pharmacy
forces.description: The Irish community pharmacy sector is experiencing active M&A and consolidation, with an estimated 98 transactions completed between 2023 and 2025. This trend, expected to continue, reflects robust investor confidence and attractive long-term fundamentals for the sector, potentially leading to larger, more efficient retail networks for branded OTC medicines and self-care products.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Dutch drugstores gaining online market share amid retail e-commerce growth
viewpoints.description: ING Research notes that Dutch e-commerce remains the primary retail growth driver, with an expected increase of 4.5% in 2026. For the first time since 2022, multichannel retailers, including drugstores, have outpaced online-only retailers in online sales growth. This trend suggests traditional retailers are regaining market share online, particularly in segments like supermarkets and drugstores, benefiting the distribution channels for OTC medicines and self-care products.
viewpoints.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

viewpoints.title: Irish community pharmacy to expand primary care role, supported by policy
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland states that community pharmacy in Ireland is expected to play an increasingly important role in primary care delivery, driven by healthcare policy supporting care in the community. This evolution follows the implementation of the Community Pharmacy Agreement and the expansion of pharmacists' clinical roles through services like the Common Conditions Service, enhancing pharmacy-led health management which includes guidance for self-medication and OTC products.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish retail sector sees stronger performance in pharmaceuticals and medical articles
viewpoints.description: Allianz IE's outlook for the Irish retail sector in Q2 2026 indicates a challenging trading environment overall, but highlights stronger performance in specific subsectors. Among these, 'Pharmaceuticals, Medical & Cosmetic Articles' recorded positive sales growth. This suggests resilient consumer spending on health and self-care products sold through retail channels, which include branded OTC medicines and self-care items, despite broader pressures on discretionary spending.

demand_drivers.description: The long-term shift towards online shopping continues, driving robust growth in e-commerce, particularly benefiting multichannel retailers like drugstores for convenient access to health products.

new_opportunities.description: Multichannel drugstores are strengthening digital capabilities and leveraging extensive physical networks to capture growing online demand for health and self-care products.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research forecasts 4.5% growth in e-commerce for 2026, making it the primary retail growth driver. Within this, online spending is growing fastest in segments like drugstores, indicating a significant digital channel for OTC and self-care products.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

demand_drivers.description: Growing demand for managing chronic diseases increases pharmacy visits and pharmacist interactions, creating opportunities for advice and sales of self-care and OTC products.

The increasing utilization of services like the Common Conditions Service expands pharmacists' roles in frontline healthcare, bolstering pharmacy-led health management and potentially increasing consumer trust and purchases of associated OTC products.

new_opportunities.description: Community pharmacies are becoming increasingly integral to primary care delivery, offering new avenues for distributing self-care products and providing health management advice.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Integration of pharmacy into primary care

market_sizing.methodology: Community pharmacy, a key channel for OTC products, saw pharmaceutical sales increase by 3.9% in Q1 2026. This, alongside growing prescription medicine values and volumes, reflects a strengthening of the pharmacy sector. The expanded clinical role of pharmacists further supports pharmacy-led health management, integral to the OTC market.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026
